close_reason: Decomposed into existing workspace execution epic bd:JMAP-grs0 (Inner-state HashMap restructure). This metadata-server-scope finding is the per-crate equivalent of bd:JMAP-x2gd.52 (chat-server scope) and bd:JMAP-x2gd.84 (cross-walk classification, closed). Epic grs0 was filed previously but had no children; this session filed 8 per-crate children (canonical jmap-mail-server at .1 with 6 known .to_owned sites, 7 siblings at .2-.8 blocking on .1). Metadata-server's grs0.8 is the bead that will land the fix in this crate. Epic adopts option (a) nested HashMap<&'static str, HashMap<String, T>> per the recommendation in grs0's epic body — outer key is &'static str (no alloc), inner HashMap<String, V>::get works with &str via Borrow<str> stdlib path. No code change made under this bead — execution moves to grs0.8 (gated by grs0.1 canonical landing first).
description:
src/memory.rs:115-124 defines Inner's storage maps with composite keys of the form (&'static str, String):

    objects: HashMap<(&'static str, String), HashMap<Id, serde_json::Value>>,
    states: HashMap<(&'static str, String), u64>,
    change_log: HashMap<(&'static str, String), Vec<ChangeEntry>>,

Every read-side lookup must allocate a String for the lookup key, because HashMap::get<Q>(&self, key: &Q) requires K: Borrow<Q>, and (&'static str, String) does not Borrow<(&str, &str)>. Witness sites:

    src/memory.rs:130: .get(&(type_name, account_id.to_owned()))
    src/memory.rs:137: .entry((type_name, account_id.to_owned()))
    src/memory.rs:148: self.known_accounts.insert(account_id.to_owned());
    src/memory.rs:150: .entry((type_name, account_id.to_owned()))
    src/memory.rs:159: self.objects.get(&(type_name, account_id.to_owned()))
    src/memory.rs:168: .entry((type_name, account_id.to_owned()))
    src/memory.rs:434: .get(&(O::TYPE_NAME, account_id.as_ref().to_owned()))
    src/memory.rs:637: inner.known_accounts.insert(account_id.as_ref().to_owned());
    src/memory.rs:853: .get(&(Metadata::TYPE_NAME, account_id.as_ref().to_owned()))

Idiomatic Rust would either:

(a) Use a nested map structure: HashMap<&'static str, HashMap<String, T>> — outer keyed by static str (no alloc), inner keyed by String but the lookup string can borrow.

(b) Use a CompactString or SmartString for the second component (still allocates, but inline for short ids).

(c) Use a typed key newtype implementing Borrow<&str> via a custom unsized type — too complex for a demo backend, but the right answer for a production backend.

(d) Accept the alloc explicitly: the canonical mail-server's MemoryBackend has the same pattern (memory.rs:131-160 across crate-jmap-mail-server). Workspace policy: this is a canonical-template issue, not a metadata-server divergence — fix in jmap-mail-server first, then propagate.

What goes wrong as-is: every /get, /changes, /set, /query call allocates a temporary String for each HashMap lookup. For the reference impl this is acceptable (the rustdoc disclaims production-grade); for downstream contributors copying the pattern into production, the demo backend telegraphs the wrong idiom. AGENTS.md says 'demo_next_id cargo-cult warning block is load-bearing onboarding documentation' (per JMAP-ayoz.20) — the same load-bearing-warning logic applies here, and there is no warning. Either fix the canonical or document the alloc as an explicit demo concession.

Priority is P3 (not P1) because: (1) it is a canonical-template issue affecting all 7 extension-server siblings equally, (2) the rustdoc explicitly disclaims this as 'not production', (3) no downstream consumer is shipping this. The fix is canonical-first per workspace AGENTS.md.
title: MemoryBackend HashMap key (&'static str, String) forces .to_owned() allocation on every lookup
